5.5
Biopsy strategy
Prostate biopsy can be performed using various strategies (systematic, targeted, etc.) and approaches (i.e.
transperineal versus transrectal).
5.5.1
Systematic biopsy strategy
For systematic biopsies in which no prior imaging is used for targeting, the sample sites should be bilateral from
apex to base, as far posterior and lateral as possible in the peripheral gland, regardless of the approach used. A
2006 SR showed that 12 is the minimum number of cores for systematic biopsies, with > 12 cores not increasing
cancer detection rate significantly [406].
5.5.2
Targeted biopsy strategy
Where MRI has shown a suspicious lesion, MR-targeted biopsy can be obtained through cognitive guidance, US/
MR fusion software or direct in-bore guidance.

interventions.body:
WHAT I FOUND
**radiology_report**: The mpMRI Prostate exam revealed a well-defined, hypointense lesion in the peripheral zone of the left posterior mid-gland, measuring approximately 18 x 14 x 16 mm. The lesion showed marked restricted diffusion on DWI (b=1400) with corresponding low ADC values. Dynamic contrast-enhanced sequences showed early, intense enhancement. No extracapsular extension or seminal vesicle invasion was identified. Impression: PI-RADS 5 lesion in the left posterior peripheral zone. Prostate volume 48.89 mL, PSA density 0.35 ng/mL/mL. Clinical stage cT1c. csPCa predicted probability 0.86317605.
**pathology_report**: The submitted prostate tissue cores showed no malignant glands. The Gleason score was 0+0, corresponding to ISUP grade group 0. No cribriform or intraductal patterns were identified. Perineural invasion was not observed. Summary of trajectory: The histological findings remain consistent with benign prostate tissue, with no evidence of malignancy or high-risk features. AI-predicted ISUP grade group (digital pathology): grade group 0.
**previous_notes**: Notes from May 2024 indicated a rise in PSA from 5.3 ng/mL to 9.5 ng/mL, prompting a repeat mpMRI. Notes from September 2024 confirmed the PI-RADS 5 lesion and referred the patient for urological re-evaluation due to the discrepancy with the prior negative biopsy.
**family_history**: Not recorded.
**psa_trend**: The PSA trend shows a trajectory of increasing PSA levels: 3.0 ng/mL in September 2022, 5.3 ng/mL in July 2023, 9.5 ng/mL in April 2024, and 17.0 ng/mL in January 2025.
**laboratory_results**: The most recent PSA is 17.0 ng/mL (as of 15 Dec 2024). Free PSA is 4.47 ng/mL (26%). Other labs (Hb, WBC, Platelets, Creatinine, eGFR, Testosterone, ALP, LDH, HbA1c) are recorded.

WHAT IS NOT RECORDED
Family history is not recorded.
